sentences.en: So much thought has gone into every little aspect of the city, starting with the street grid itself.
sentences.zh: 城市的每一个细微之处都凝聚了无数的心思，从街道网格本身开始。

sentences.en: So, in 1830, before Chicago even existed, the state of Illinois decided to lay out plots along the Chicago River
sentences.zh: 所以，在1830年，甚至在芝加哥诞生之前，伊利诺伊州就决定沿芝加哥河划分地块

sentences.en: to sell in order to help pay for the canal that was going to connect Lake Michigan to the Mississippi.
sentences.zh: 进行出售，以此来帮助筹集连接密歇根湖和密西西比河的运河资金。

sentences.en: So, surveyor James Thompson drew the first platt.
sentences.zh: 于是，测量员詹姆斯·汤普森绘制了第一张规划图。

sentences.en: That's what it's called.

sentences.en: It's called a platt.

sentences.en: Platt.

sentences.en: And that platt was the foundation of how Chicago streets are laid out today.
sentences.zh: 那张规划图就是今天芝加哥街道布局的基础。

sentences.en: So, he drew straight streets uniformly, 66 feet wide, which was actually the full length of a surveyor's chain.
sentences.zh: 因此，他规划了笔直且宽度统一的街道，宽66英尺，这实际上正是一条测量员铁链的全长。

sentences.en: So, he just kind of like as big as possible.
sentences.zh: 所以他只是随心所欲地画得尽可能大。

sentences.en: And then alleys are 16 feet wide, bisecting each block.
sentences.zh: 接着是宽16英尺的巷子，将每个街区一分为二。

sentences.en: And any building that was already, you know, there, that was already built, that was in the way of his streets,
sentences.zh: 任何已经在那里的、已经建好的、挡住他规划街道的建筑物，

sentences.en: they were forced to move to fit on the grid, which wasn't that big of a deal in 1830

sentences.en: because only like 300 people lived in Chicago at the time, or pre-Chicago at the time.
sentences.zh: 因为当时芝加哥，或者说史前芝加哥，只有大约300人居住。

sentences.en: In 10 years, it would be 10 times that in Chicago.
sentences.zh: 十年后，芝加哥的人口将是这个数字的十倍。

sentences.en: That original platt was only a half a mile in area.
sentences.zh: 最初的那张规划图面积只有半平方英里。

sentences.en: But over two centuries, Chicago grew in exactly the way Thompson laid out that uniform regular spacing,
sentences.zh: 但在两个世纪里，芝加哥完全按照汤普森规划的那种均匀规律的间距发展着，

sentences.en: and it eventually encompassed over 230 square miles.
sentences.zh: 并最终占地超过230平方英里。

sentences.en: It's as close as any city is to a true mathematical grid.
sentences.zh: 它是最接近完美数学网格的城市。

sentences.zh: 如果你透过帽店的展示窗看进去，你会发现墙壁超级厚。

sentences.en: Like, that's not just, like, a frame.
sentences.zh: 就像，那不只是一个框架。

sentences.en: That's, like, actually the wall.
sentences.zh: 那实际上就是墙。

sentences.en: It has to be that thick.
sentences.zh: 它必须得那么厚。

sentences.en: It's about, it's about, it's about six feet wide at the base.
sentences.zh: 它大约，大约，大约在底部有六英尺宽。

sentences.en: And about 18 inches wide at the top.
sentences.zh: 顶部大约有18英寸宽。

sentences.en: And this is all because, you know, for it to have, yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是因为，你知道的，为了让它拥有，对，完全正确。

sentences.en: That's bigger than your arMs.
sentences.zh: 这比你的胳膊还要粗。

sentences.en: And then, and then little tiny.
sentences.zh: 然后，然后变得很小很小。

sentences.en: And so this is necessary because all the weight of the upper floors have to be, like, held by the bricks at the bottom.
sentences.zh: 所以这是必要的，因为上层楼的所有重量都必须由底部的砖块来承载。

sentences.en: And so they have to be super wide to sort of, to support everything up above.
sentences.zh: 所以它们必须超级宽，以便支撑上方的一切。

sentences.en: And it makes it, like, kind of like a pyramid.
sentences.zh: 这让它看起来有点像金字塔。

sentences.en: I mean, not, you know, not, it's obviously not as dramatic and it only swings out a little bit.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，不是，你知道的，不是，它显然没有那么夸张，而且向外扩展得只有一点点。

sentences.en: But if it wasn't for steel frame construction, all buildings would be pyramids if they ever got, if they got tall enough.
sentences.zh: 但如果不是因为钢框架结构，所有建筑如果建得足够高的话，都会变成金字塔。

sentences.en: Because what you mostly see when you see bricks on the surface of buildings are not structural bricks.
sentences.zh: 因为当你看到建筑物表面有砖时，你大片看到的并不是结构砖。

sentences.en: They're like skin.
sentences.zh: 它们就像皮肤一样。

sentences.en: They're like, there's a steel frame and they put bricks over it to make it look like a brick building.
sentences.zh: 它们就像，里面有一个钢框架，外面铺上砖来让它看起来像一栋砖砌建筑。

sentences.en: But it's not made of bricks inside.
sentences.zh: 但它内部并不是用砖砌成的。

sentences.en: So, actually, the southern half of this building has some modern construction with some frames in it.
sentences.zh: 所以，实际上，这座建筑的南半部分有一些现代建筑结构，里面带有一些框架。

sentences.en: But this part is completely masonry.
sentences.zh: 但这一部分完全是砌体结构。

sentences.en: And that's why it is so weird.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么它这么奇特。

sentences.en: And kind of that heaviness you feel, you know, it's kind of cool.
sentences.zh: 而且你感受到的那种厚重感，你知道的，还挺酷的。

sentences.en: But it's because of the way it was built.
sentences.zh: 但这全是因为它的建造方式。

sentences.en: It's also, like, really dark brick, which is just like a choice.
sentences.zh: 而且它也是非常深的砖色，这纯粹是一种设计选择。

sentences.en: So, I want to get to two other buildings that are my favorite buildings.
sentences.zh: 所以，我想去另外两栋我最喜欢的建筑。

sentences.en: And they're just north of the river, which is not too far from here.
sentences.zh: 它们就在河的北面，离这里不太远。

sentences.en: But on the way there, I want to check out the sign on the Chicago Theater.
sentences.zh: 但在去那里的路上，我想看看芝加哥剧院的招牌。

sentences.en: On the marquee behind the middle C of the word Chicago, okay, is a Y-shaped symbol.
sentences.zh: 在“Chicago”这个词中间字母C后面的大招牌上，好吗，有一个Y字形的标志。

sentences.en: You can kind of miss it, but it's this Y-shaped symbol.
sentences.zh: 你可能会错过它，但它确实是一个Y字形的标志。

sentences.en: And this is what's called the municipal device of Chicago.
sentences.zh: 这就是所谓的芝加哥市徽。

sentences.en: It's a simplified map of Chicago that shows the river splitting into the north and south branches.
sentences.zh: 它是芝加哥的简化地图，显示了河流分叉成南北两支。

sentences.en: That's what the Y comes from.
sentences.zh: 这就是Y字的由来。

sentences.en: Since 1917, this has been the official symbol of the city.
sentences.zh: 自1917年以来，这一直是该市的官方标志。

sentences.en: And it's been used on official buildings and on, you know, city vehicles and stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 它一直被用于官方建筑上，还有，你知道的，城市车辆等等。

sentences.en: I noticed it a lot on control boxes and, like, the gates of parks and stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 我经常在控制箱上看到它，还有公园的大门之类的东西上。

sentences.en: You'll see a Y there.
sentences.zh: 你会看到那里有一个Y字。

sentences.en: And that means Chicago.
sentences.zh: 这就代表芝加哥。

sentences.en: It was used a lot in the beginning of the 20th century, less so later on.
sentences.zh: 它在20世纪初被广泛使用，后来就少一些了。

sentences.en: You wouldn't see it as much as the city of Chicago flag, like, around the city.
sentences.zh: 在城市里，你不会像看到芝加哥市旗那样频繁地看到它。

sentences.en: But you'll find Y's everywhere.
sentences.zh: 但到处都能找到Y字。

sentences.en: And so, it's kind of fun to do a little scavenger hunt for Y's around.
sentences.zh: 所以，四处寻找Y字来玩一场小型寻宝游戏还挺有趣的。

sentences.en: And so, we should do that while we're here.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们在这里的时候应该也玩一下。

sentences.en: You like a scavenger hunt.
sentences.zh: 你喜欢寻宝游戏。

sentences.en: I do.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢。

sentences.en: I do love a good scavenger hunt.
sentences.zh: 我确实很喜欢一个精彩的寻宝游戏。

sentences.en: I mean, because life moves pretty faSt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，因为生活节奏太快了。

sentences.en: And if you don't stop and look around once in a while, you could miss it.
sentences.zh: 如果你不偶尔停下脚步四处看看，你可能会错过它。

sentences.en: So, this gorgeous thing right here is the Wrigley building.
sentences.zh: 所以，眼前这个华丽的家伙就是瑞格利大厦。

sentences.en: And it is so fancy.
sentences.zh: 它实在是太豪华了。

sentences.en: It is covered in white terracotta.
sentences.zh: 它覆盖着白色的饰面砖。

sentences.en: It has that great silver sky bridge in the middle, which I really love that thing, actually.
sentences.zh: 中间有一座很棒的银色空中走廊，实际上我真的很喜欢那个东西。

sentences.en: And what I can't get over when it comes to this thing is that this was all bought and paid for with chewing gum money.
sentences.zh: 而且说到这东西，最让我惊叹的是，这全部是用口香糖的钱买下来并支付的。

sentences.en: It was designed as the Wrigley headquarters.
sentences.zh: 它被设计为瑞格利公司的总部。

sentences.en: Construction started in 1920.
sentences.zh: 始建于1920年。

sentences.en: Wrigley was kind of late to the chewing gum game.
sentences.zh: 瑞格利进入口香糖行业的时间有点晚。

sentences.en: He was this serial entrepreneur.
sentences.zh: 他是一位连续创业者。

sentences.en: So, he sold soap.
sentences.zh: 所以，他卖过肥皂。

sentences.en: And as a promotion, he would give away baking powder with the purchase of the soap.
sentences.zh: 作为促销手段，他会在购买肥皂时赠送发酵粉。

sentences.en: And then it turned out that the baking powder was more popular than the soap.
sentences.zh: 结果发酵粉比肥皂更受欢迎。

sentences.en: So, he started selling the baking powder.
sentences.zh: 于是他开始卖发酵粉。

sentences.en: And then, as a promotion for the baking powder, he started giving away sticks of chewing gum inside the baking powder.
sentences.zh: 然后，作为发酵粉的促销活动，他开始在发酵粉里面赠送口香糖条。

sentences.en: And then he learned that the sticks of chewing gum were more popular than the baking powder.
sentences.zh: 接着他发现口香糖条比发酵粉更受欢迎。

sentences.en: And so, he just started selling chewing gum from there.
sentences.zh: 所以，从那以后他就开始只卖口香糖了。

sentences.en: When he found chewing gum, he found his true calling.
sentences.zh: 当他找到口香糖时，他找到了自己真正的使命。

sentences.en: And it paid for this building.
sentences.zh: 它支付了这座建筑的费用。

sentences.en: It paid for, like, Wrigley Field is named after Wrigley.
sentences.zh: 它支付了，就像瑞格利球场就是以瑞格利命名的。

sentences.en: I just find that so kind of amazing how much people spent on chewing gum during the turn of the century.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得这太不可思议了，在世纪之交人们在口香糖上花了那么多钱。

sentences.en: I sure did.
sentences.zh: 我确实这么觉得。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好。

sentences.en: So, are you tired?
sentences.zh: 那么，你累了吗？

sentences.en: Do you want to give up?
sentences.zh: 你想放弃吗？

sentences.en: Or are you thirsty for more?
sentences.zh: 还是你还想了解更多？

sentences.en: I'm thirsty for more.
sentences.zh: 我还想了解更多。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好。

sentences.en: So, then let's turn over here and cross the street.
sentences.zh: 那么我们转过这里过马路吧。

sentences.en: This is one of my favorite buildings.
sentences.zh: 这是我最喜欢的建筑之一。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好。

sentences.en: This is the Tribune Tower.
sentences.zh: 这是论坛报大厦。

sentences.en: And when I lived here, it was home of the Chicago Tribune.
sentences.zh: 当我住在这里时，它是《芝加哥论坛报》的所在地。

sentences.en: Now, it's the private apartments.
sentences.zh: 现在，它是私人公寓。

sentences.en: Actually, that was kind of a surprise to me until I was doing some research before.
sentences.zh: 说实话，这对我来说有点惊讶，直到我之前做了一些研究。

sentences.en: This building is the result of a design competition that was held in 1922.
sentences.zh: 这座建筑是1922年举办的一场设计竞赛的结果。

sentences.en: It's this sort of neo-Gothic vertical line skyscraper on the bottom.
sentences.zh: 它底部是那种新哥特式垂直线条的摩天大楼。

sentences.en: And it has this, like, Gothic cathedral hat on its head.
sentences.zh: 头顶戴着一顶哥特式大教堂帽子般的结构。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: There's a lot going on up there.
sentences.zh: 上面有很多繁复的装饰。

sentences.en: There's a lot.
sentences.zh: 有很多。

sentences.en: It even has, like, flying buttresses up there on the top.
sentences.zh: 它上面甚至还有飞扶壁。

sentences.en: On, like, a real cathedral, those buttresses would hold up the walls.
sentences.zh: 在真正的大教堂上，这些扶壁用来支撑墙壁。

sentences.en: But here, they don't do anything.
sentences.zh: 但在这里，它们什么也不做。

sentences.en: They're just there to look like cathedral buttresses.
sentences.zh: 它们呆在那里只是为了看起来像大教堂的扶壁。

sentences.en: They're kind of silly.
sentences.zh: 它们有点傻气。

sentences.en: They're just decorative.
sentences.zh: 它们纯粹是装饰性的。

sentences.en: It is this extremely weird monstrosity of a building.
sentences.zh: 它是一座极其怪异、庞大而畸形的建筑。

sentences.en: Like, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 就像，我不知道。

sentences.en: Like, I kind of like it.
sentences.zh: 就像，我其实还蛮喜欢它的。

sentences.en: Yeah, I like it, too.
sentences.zh: 对，我也喜欢它。

sentences.en: Yeah, so, I mean, I kind of like it.
sentences.zh: 对，所以，我的意思是，我挺喜欢它的。

sentences.en: But, like, its problem was that when this design competition was happening,
sentences.zh: 但是，它的问题在于，当这场设计竞赛举行的时候，

sentences.en: modernism was just getting going, really.
sentences.zh: 现代主义其实才刚刚兴起。

sentences.en: And skyscraper architecture was celebrating, you know, clean lines and simplicity.
sentences.zh: 而摩天大楼建筑当时正在推崇简洁的线条和朴素的风格。

sentences.en: And then this design won the conteSt.
sentences.zh: 结果这个设计赢得了竞赛。

sentences.en: And the sort of forward-thinking critics just hated it.
sentences.zh: 那些具有前瞻性的评论家简直恨透了它。

sentences.en: But, you know, I think it's all right.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我觉得还好。

sentences.en: I think it's interesting, you know, at leaSt.
sentences.zh: 至少我觉得它挺有趣的。

sentences.en: Now, what's really cool is the building that isn't here.
sentences.zh: 现在，真正酷的是那座并没有被建造出来的建筑。

sentences.en: The second place finisher of this design competition from the Chicago Tribune architecture contest
sentences.zh: 在芝加哥论坛报建筑竞赛中获得第二名的设计，

sentences.en: was a design by Aleel Saarinen.
sentences.zh: 是埃利尔·沙里宁的设计。

sentences.en: And he was this Finnish architect.
sentences.zh: 他是一位芬兰建筑师。

sentences.en: And he's the father of Iro Saarinen, who became one of the most important architects of the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 他是埃罗·沙里宁的父亲，而埃罗后来成为了20世纪最重要的建筑师之一。

sentences.en: So Aleel Saarinen's Tribune Tower design, it won $20,000 as a second-placed finisher.
sentences.zh: 所以埃利尔·沙里宁的论坛报大厦设计作为亚军赢得了2万美元。

sentences.en: It was never built, but the design was shared with the public.
sentences.zh: 它从未被建造，但该设计与公众分享了。

sentences.en: And those critics who hated the winning design, they flipped for this tower, Saarinen's Tower.
sentences.zh: 那些讨厌获胜设计的评论家们，对沙里宁的这座大厦狂热不已。

sentences.en: It was this soaring setback tower, had these strong vertical lines.
sentences.zh: 这是一座高耸且带有退台式结构的大厦，有着强烈的垂直线条。

sentences.en: It had a huge effect on 20th century architecture.
sentences.zh: 它对20世纪的建筑产生了巨大的影响。

sentences.en: It influenced a bunch of skyscrapers all over the country.
sentences.zh: 它影响了全国各地的一批摩天大楼。

sentences.en: And it's probably the most important silver medalist ever, next to Nancy Kerrigan.
sentences.zh: 它可能是除了南希·克雷根之外，历史上最重要的银牌得主。

sentences.en: So that was the first silver medalist I could think of.
sentences.zh: 这就是我能想到的第一个银牌得主。

sentences.en: But Saarinen's design was way more important than this building, even though this building got built.
sentences.zh: 但沙里宁的设计比这座实际建成的建筑重要得多，尽管这座建筑确实建成了。

sentences.en: It has way more effect in the world.
sentences.zh: 它对世界产生了更大的影响。

sentences.en: I find that really fascinating.
sentences.zh: 我发现这真的非常吸引人。

sentences.en: But the best thing about this weird goth building that actually got built is not the architecture itself,
sentences.zh: 但这座实际建成的怪异哥特式建筑最棒的地方不是建筑本身，

sentences.en: but the architecture embedded on the side of it, which we have to get up close to see.
sentences.zh: 而是嵌入它侧面的那些建筑碎片，我们必须走近才能看到它们。

sentences.en: So all along the first floor of the Tribune Tower, you'll see these little bits and bricks and fragments of other buildings from around the world.
sentences.zh: 所以在论坛报大厦的一楼沿街，你会看到来自世界各地其他建筑的小块砖块和碎片。

sentences.en: It's this little museum just on the street here.
sentences.zh: 这就像是街头的一个小小博物馆。

sentences.en: So when Colonel McCormick was the publisher of the Tribune in the 1920s, he encouraged his foreign correspondents,
sentences.zh: 所以当麦考密克上校在20世纪20年代担任《论坛报》出版商时，他鼓励他的海外通讯员，

sentences.en: I guess you could say generously, to collect artifacts from around the world.
sentences.zh: 我想可以说是慷慨地鼓励他们，去收集来自世界各地的文物。

sentences.en: He asked to steal them and bring them back.
sentences.zh: 他要求把它们偷回来并带回国。

sentences.en: He had a nice little collection.
sentences.zh: 他有一个不错的小收藏。

sentences.en: Some people sent them, whether it be demolitions or extensive rehabs of historical places.
sentences.zh: 有些人将它们寄了过来，无论是来自历史遗迹的拆除还是大规模翻新。

sentences.en: Knowing that McCormick collected these, they would send them to him.
sentences.zh: 既然知道麦考密克在收集这些东西，他们就会把它们寄给他。

sentences.en: So some of them were probably gotten above board, but I think they were mostly stolen.
sentences.zh: 所以其中一些可能是通过正当途径获得的，但我觉得大部分都是偷来的。

sentences.en: So they had this collection.
sentences.zh: 所以他们有了这个藏品。

sentences.en: And so when the building was finished in 1925, they embedded them in the facade with plaques indicating what they were called and their place of origin.
sentences.zh: 因此，当这栋建筑于1925年完工时，他们将这些东西嵌入了外墙，并配有铭牌，标明它们的名称和产地。

sentences.en: And it's been added to over the decades as well.
sentences.zh: 而且在过去的几十年里，它还在不断增加。

sentences.en: So if you walk around there, you can see pieces of really amazing sites.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你在那附近走走，你能看到一些真正令人惊叹的建筑遗迹。

sentences.en: So like Taj Mahal, the Alamo, the Great Pyramid, and the Great Wall of China up there.
sentences.zh: 比如泰姬陵、阿拉莫、大金字塔和中国的万里长城都在上面。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm pretty sure that's one of those ones that wasn't taken with anyone's knowledge.
sentences.zh: 对，我敢肯定那是一个在无人知晓的情况下被拿走的东西。

sentences.en: There's the Berlin Wall here too.
sentences.zh: 这里也有柏林墙。

sentences.en: And then around the corner here, this is the one that always sort of struck me,
sentences.zh: 然后在这边的拐角处，这个是我一直觉得有点触动我的地方，

sentences.en: is that there's even like a twisted piece of metal from the World Trade Center Towers,
sentences.zh: 就是甚至还有一块来自世界贸易中心双子塔的扭曲金属，

sentences.en: which really kind of, it kind of surprised me and I find it notable and interesting.
sentences.zh: 这真的让我有点惊讶，我觉得它很显眼也很有趣。

sentences.en: It's sort of behind the scaffolding there, but it's really different than all the other pieces.
sentences.zh: 它有点在那种脚手架后面，但它和所有其他部分真的很不一样。

sentences.en: Most of the pieces are pieces of stone and cornices, and this is the piece of metal.
sentences.zh: 大部分部分都是石头和檐口，而这是一块金属。

sentences.en: Okay, so this next thing isn't specific to Chicago, so you can appreciate this whatever city you're in,
sentences.zh: 好吧，这接下来的一点并非芝加哥所独有，所以无论你在哪个城市都能体会到这一点，

sentences.en: but it's a very big feature, I think, in Chicago, and that's all the revolving doors.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得这是芝加哥一个非常大的特色，那就是所有的旋转门。

sentences.en: Did you notice all the revolving doors?
sentences.zh: 你注意到所有的旋转门了吗？

sentences.en: I did.
sentences.zh: 我注意到了。

sentences.en: Yeah, so like everything has a revolving door.
sentences.zh: 对，好像每样东西都有旋转门。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The revolving door is really important to Chicago because of all the extreme weather.
sentences.zh: 旋转门对芝加哥非常重要，因为这里有极端的天气。

sentences.en: But they were introduced to America from Germany by Theophilus van Kennel in the late 1800s,
sentences.zh: 但它们是在19世纪末由狄奥菲勒斯·范·肯尔从德国引入美国的，

sentences.en: and he started this revolving door company.
sentences.zh: 他创办了这家旋转门公司。

sentences.en: And it advertised the doors as,
sentences.zh: 它对这些门的宣传是，

sentences.en: they cannot be left open, blown open, or slammed.
sentences.zh: 它们不会被敞开、被风吹开或被猛然关上。

sentences.en: They're always closed, yet allowing the passage of persons.
sentences.zh: 它们总是关闭的，但同时又允许人员通行。

sentences.en: In other words, they're always open, always closed,
sentences.zh: 换句话说，它们总是开着的，也总是关着的，

sentences.en: which is a big deal in a city like Chicago with its extreme weather.
sentences.zh: 这在像芝加哥这样天气极端的城市里是一件大事。

sentences.en: So every time a conventional swinging door is opened,
sentences.zh: 所以每次传统的平开门被打开时，

sentences.en: the HVAC system has to compensate,
sentences.zh: 暖通空调系统就必须进行补偿，

sentences.en: and that wastes thousands of dollars of energy costs per year.
sentences.zh: 这每年会浪费数千美元的能源成本。

sentences.en: So there are lots of revolving doors here.
sentences.zh: 所以这里有很多旋转门。

sentences.en: But here's the thing.
sentences.zh: 但问题是这样的。

sentences.en: I mean, how do you feel about using revolving doors?
sentences.zh: 我是说，你对使用旋转门有什么感觉？

sentences.en: I find them difficult.
sentences.zh: 我觉得它们很难用。

sentences.en: Yes, so most people do.
sentences.zh: 是的，大多数人都有同感。

sentences.en: This is normal.
sentences.zh: 这是正常的。

sentences.en: I thought it was just me.
sentences.zh: 我还以为只有我这样呢。

sentences.en: No, no, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不。

sentences.en: So for safety reasons,
sentences.zh: 所以出于安全原因，

sentences.en: there's always a conventional door beside revolving doors.
sentences.zh: 旋转门旁边总会有一扇传统的门。

sentences.en: And most people don't really like revolving doors all that much
sentences.zh: 而且大多数人其实并不是那么喜欢旋转门，

sentences.en: because they feel claustrophobic, they feel weird.
sentences.zh: 因为它们会让人感到幽闭恐惧，让人觉得怪怪的。

sentences.en: You know, it's just one of those things.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就是那种让人无奈的事物之一。

sentences.en: So buildings use a lot of signage to kind of nudge people
sentences.zh: 所以建筑会使用大量的标牌来引导人们

sentences.en: into using the revolving door.
sentences.zh: 去使用旋转门。

sentences.en: And at fancy buildings, the doorman will like start it swinging, you know?
sentences.zh: 在高级的建筑里，门童会帮你把它转动起来，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Give it a little nudge or push.
sentences.zh: 轻轻推它一下。

sentences.en: Exactly, so that you jump into it rather than...
sentences.zh: 没错，好让你顺势跨进去，而不是……

sentences.en: They don't put a person usually on the swinging door.
sentences.zh: 通常他们不会在平开门旁安排专人。

sentences.en: You have to do that one yourself.
sentences.zh: 那扇门你得自己推。

sentences.en: But if you follow the doorman's suggestion,
sentences.zh: 但如果你听从门童的建议，

sentences.en: you'll go through the revolving door.
sentences.zh: 你就会穿过旋转门。

sentences.en: So revolving doors are really great.
sentences.zh: 所以旋转门真的很棒。

sentences.en: They're there for a reason.
sentences.zh: 它们的存在是有原因的。

sentences.en: And you should try to use them in terms of like energy usage if you can.
sentences.zh: 如果可以的话，从能源消耗的角度来看，你应该尽量使用它们。

sentences.en: But it's totally normal that if you feel like that's uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 但如果你觉得这很不舒服，这也是完全正常的。

sentences.en: The other way they try to make them better is as they got bigger,
sentences.zh: 他们试图改进它们的另一种方法是，随着它们变得越来越大，

sentences.en: they're kind of less claustrophobic.
sentences.zh: 它们的幽闭恐惧感就会减少一些。

sentences.en: But older buildings, like a lot of them around here,
sentences.zh: 但较旧的建筑，就像这里的很多建筑一样，

sentences.en: are still like little revolving doors, which feel uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 仍然是那种用起来让人感到不舒服的小型旋转门。

sentences.en: So I want to show you one thing that's significant,
sentences.zh: 所以我向你展示一个意义重大、

sentences.en: but maybe a little more abstract that points to why
sentences.zh: 但可能稍微抽象一点的事物，它指向了为什么

sentences.en: I think Chicago is this paragon of design.
sentences.zh: 我认为芝加哥是这种设计典范的原因。

sentences.en: But I want to cross over here
sentences.zh: 但我想从这里穿过去，

sentences.en: because there's a lot of cops.
sentences.zh: 因为有很多警察。

sentences.en: There's a lot of cops in Chicago, actually.
sentences.zh: 事实上，芝加哥有很多警察。

sentences.en: And I'm unpopular with the Chicago Police Department.
sentences.zh: 而且我在芝加哥警察局很不受欢迎。

sentences.en: Why are you so unpopular with the Chicago Police Department?
sentences.zh: 为什么你在芝加哥警察局这么不受欢迎？

sentences.en: So that building standing alone near Navy Pier,
sentences.zh: 所以那栋孤零零地耸立在海军码头附近的建筑，

sentences.en: that's Navy Pier, like extending out into the lake.
sentences.zh: 那就是海军码头，像这样延伸到湖里。

sentences.en: That building, that tall building, is Lake Point Tower.
sentences.zh: 那栋建筑，那栋高楼，就是湖点大厦。

sentences.en: And if you notice, it is the only skyscraper east of Lakeshore Drive.
sentences.zh: 如果你注意的话，它是湖滨大道以东唯一的摩天大楼。

sentences.en: It's doing its own thing.
sentences.zh: 它在走自己的路。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And Lakeshore Drive is this like big parkway that runs along Lake Michigan.
sentences.zh: 湖滨大道是沿着密歇根湖延伸的一条宽阔林荫大道。

sentences.en: There was already a city ordinance that limited construction east of Lakeshore Drive.
sentences.zh: 当时已经有一项城市条例限制在湖滨大道以东进行建设。

sentences.en: But this building kind of snuck in through a loophole.
sentences.zh: 但这栋建筑算是通过一个漏洞钻了进来。

sentences.en: Luckily, it's a pretty nice building.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，它是一栋相当不错的建筑。

sentences.en: So it's okay.
sentences.zh: 所以这倒也无所谓。

sentences.en: That loophole was definitively closed in 1971 with the Lake Front Protection Ordinance,
sentences.zh: 1971年通过《湖滨保护条例》，这个漏洞被彻底堵住了，

sentences.en: which banned all commercial construction by the lake.
sentences.zh: 该条例禁止在湖畔进行所有商业建设。

sentences.en: When I lived here, Chicago Tribune columnist Eric Zorn made a list of all the best architectural features in Chicago.
sentences.zh: 我住在这里时，《芝加哥论坛报》专栏作家埃里克·佐恩列出了芝加哥所有最好的建筑特色。

sentences.en: And he cited the Lake Front Ordinance as one of the top pieces of quote-unquote architecture in Chicago,
sentences.zh: 他将《湖滨条例》列为芝加哥所谓的顶级“建筑”杰作之一，

sentences.en: which was such a cool idea to me.
sentences.zh: 这在我看来是一个绝妙的想法。

sentences.en: The lakefront didn't get cluttered up and cut off from the average person with this dense cluster of waterfront towers or docks.
sentences.zh: 凭借这片密集的滨水高楼或码头，湖滨没有变得拥挤不堪并与普通人隔绝。

sentences.en: And that insight about what made Chicago so good kind of blew my mind.
sentences.zh: 而关于是什么让芝加哥如此美好的这一深刻见解，简直让我大开眼界。

sentences.en: Like, it sort of made me think about cities in a totally different way.
sentences.zh: 比如，它让我以一种完全不同的方式去思考城市。

sentences.en: This place is known as the epicenter of skyscraper design for the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 这个地方被称为20世纪摩天大楼设计中心。

sentences.en: And the buildings, of course, have a lot to do with it.
sentences.zh: 当然，这些建筑在其中起了很大作用。

sentences.en: But I also think it's kind of how the whole city works together, that it's key architectural strength.
sentences.zh: 但我也认为，整座城市如何协同运作才是其核心的建筑优势。

sentences.en: Like, the space and the vistas and the vantage points make observing and appreciating the architecture all the better.
sentences.zh: 例如，空间、远景和观景点使得观察和欣赏建筑变得更加美妙。

sentences.en: Like, New York has amazing buildings.
sentences.zh: 就像纽约拥有惊人的建筑一样。

sentences.en: I know you love New York.
sentences.zh: 我知道你爱纽约。

sentences.en: I'm not competing, like, there's no competition between Chicago and New York.
sentences.zh: 我不是在比较，芝加哥和纽约之间没有竞争。

sentences.en: It has amazing buildings.
sentences.zh: 它拥有惊人的建筑。

sentences.en: But they're all kind of crammed in on narrow streets.
sentences.zh: 但它们都挤在狭窄的街道上。

sentences.en: And I appreciate that density.
sentences.zh: 我很欣赏那种密度。

sentences.en: It works really well for New York.
sentences.zh: 它对纽约非常有效。

sentences.en: But you could be, like, walking along and all of a sudden the Chrysler building's in front of you.
sentences.zh: 但你可能正走着走着，突然克莱斯勒大厦就出现在你面前了。

sentences.en: And I could miss it.
sentences.zh: 而我可能会错过它。

sentences.en: You know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 你知道我的意思吗？

sentences.en: It's kind of a strange thing.
sentences.zh: 这有点奇怪。

sentences.en: And it could really surprise you.
sentences.zh: 而且它真的会吓你一跳。

sentences.en: But all these ordinances and, you know, conventions and respect for the whole somehow elevates Chicago.
sentences.zh: 但所有这些条例、习俗以及对整体的尊重，不知何故提升了芝加哥的品位。

sentences.en: Like, the buildings talk to each other.
sentences.zh: 就像这些建筑在彼此对话一样。

sentences.en: A skyscraper from the 1990s will borrow and modify a motif from a neighboring building that was erected, like, 70 years before.
sentences.zh: 一座20世纪90年代的摩天大楼会借鉴并修改70年前建造的邻近建筑的主题。

sentences.en: The NBC building has buttresses on it because it's right next to the Chicago Tribune.
sentences.zh: NBC大楼上有扶壁，因为它紧邻芝加哥论坛报大楼。

sentences.en: And so the Tribune Tower had buttresses at the top that did nothing.
sentences.zh: 所以论坛报大楼顶部有实际上毫无用处的扶壁。

sentences.en: The NBC building has buttresses that actually do something.
sentences.zh: NBC大楼上的扶壁则是真正起作用的。

sentences.en: But they're there because of the other buttresses.
sentences.zh: 但它们之所以存在，是因为有那些其他的扶壁。

sentences.en: And having that space across a plaza, across the river, allows for that cross-generational conversation.
sentences.zh: 而且通过广场、跨过河流拥有这种空间，才使得跨代对话成为可能。

sentences.en: And it's just made possible because of the simple fact that we can see it all together.
sentences.zh: 这仅仅是因为一个简单的事实：我们可以把它们全貌尽收眼底。

sentences.en: That architects really cared how everything looked and worked together.
sentences.zh: 建筑师们真的很关心一切看起来和运作起来是否协调一致。

sentences.en: And that's why Chicago, to me, is a city like no other.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么在我看来，芝加哥是一座无与伦比的城市。

sentences.en: And things like the Lakefront Ordinance are a part of that.
sentences.zh: 诸如《湖滨条例》之类的事物正是其中的一部分。

sentences.en: It's like a respect for taking in the hole and having this cohesive city in terms of its architecture and design.
sentences.zh: 这就像是对审视整体的一种尊重，在建筑和设计方面拥有一座具有凝聚力的城市。

sentences.en: So this is, like, the exception that proves the rule, this, like, building standing outside of the normal rules.
sentences.zh: 所以这是证明规则的例外，这座打破常规的建筑，

sentences.en: But luckily, again, it's a pretty good-looking building, you know.
sentences.zh: 但幸运的是，它依然是一座相当好看的建筑。

sentences.en: Sounds like that deserves a star on the flag.
sentences.zh: 听起来这值得在旗帜上加一颗星。

sentences.en: The Lakefront Ordinance does, for sure.
sentences.zh: 《湖滨条例》绝对值得。

sentences.en: I think so, too.
sentences.zh: 我也这么认为。

sentences.en: Okay, so I want to go to our last stop.
sentences.zh: 好了，我想去我们的最后一站。

sentences.en: We're already at our last stop.
sentences.zh: 我们已经到最后一站了。

sentences.en: I want to take us to my favorite building.
sentences.zh: 我想带大家去我最喜欢的建筑。

sentences.en: Oh, your favorite building.
sentences.zh: 哦，你最喜欢的建筑。

sentences.en: And it's kind of the building that kind of started it all for me.
sentences.zh: 可以说就是这栋建筑为我开启了一切。

sentences.en: But to get there, we have to go the Chicago way.
sentences.zh: 但要到那里，我们必须走“芝加哥方式”。

sentences.en: What's the Chicago way?
sentences.zh: 什么是“芝加哥方式”？

sentences.en: They pull a knife, you pull a gun.
sentences.zh: 他们动刀子，你就要掏枪。

sentences.en: He sends one of yours to the hospital, you send one of his to the morgue.
sentences.zh: 他把你们的人送进医院，你就要把他们的人送进太平间。

sentences.en: That's the Chicago way.
sentences.zh: 这就是“芝加哥方式”。

sentences.en: But in this specific case, I mean taking Chicago Avenue west to where it meets the north branch of the river.
sentences.zh: 但在这种具体情况下，我的意思是沿着芝加哥大道向西，直到它与河流北支交汇的地方。

sentences.en: We'll get there after the break.
sentences.zh: 休息之后我们将到达那里。

sentences.en: This special bonus episode of 99% Invisible is brought to you by the 2024 Lexus GX and Sirius XM.
sentences.zh: 本期99%无形隐蔽学的特别优选节目由2024款雷克萨斯GX和Sirius XM为您呈现。

sentences.en: The Lexus GX is at the apex of high-end luxury and high-end utility.
sentences.zh: 雷克萨斯GX处于高端奢华与高端实用性的巅峰。

sentences.en: Even though you can totally imagine the GX sitting in a corporate parking lot,
sentences.zh: 尽管你完全可以想象GX停在公司停车场的情景，

sentences.en: another passionate group found the GX and claimed it as this highly capable, reliable, modifiable, and luxurious off-road and overlanding vehicle.
sentences.zh: 另一个充满热情的群体发现了GX，并将其誉为这款功能强大、可靠、可改装且奢华的越野和长途旅行车。

sentences.en: People ask, what is overlanding?
sentences.zh: 人们会问，什么是长途越野（overlanding）？

sentences.en: And you'll ask 10 people and you'll have 10 different answers.
sentences.zh: 你问10个人，就会得到10种不同的答案。

sentences.en: Well, I'll give you my definition.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我来给出我的定义。

sentences.en: It's a fancy word for sleeping out in the boonies in your car.
sentences.zh: 这是一个时髦的词，意思就是在荒郊野岭里睡在你的车里。

sentences.en: Getting off the grid and knowing that you have the capability to go off the grid.
sentences.zh: 远离喧嚣，并且知道自己有能力去征服荒野。

sentences.en: That is Eric Cavanaugh from Lexus.
sentences.zh: 这是来自雷克萨斯的埃里克·卡瓦纳。

sentences.en: We had a fun time geeking out about all the GX could do on all these different terrains,
sentences.zh: 我们度过了一段开心的时光，狂热地探讨了GX在各种不同地形上所能做的一切，

sentences.en: even though we were idling on a roof of a parking garage on Goose Island in the middle of Chicago.
sentences.zh: 尽管当时我们正闲停在芝加哥市中心鹅岛一个停车场的屋顶上。

sentences.en: One of the features that comes standard on the Overtrail model is multi-terrain select.
sentences.zh: 越野版（Overtrail）车型标配的功能之一是多地形选择系统。

sentences.en: So you'll see here, this now unlocks a variety of different settings to help you navigate those terrains better.
sentences.zh: 所以你会在这里看到，这现在解锁了各种不同的设置，以帮助你更好地应对这些地形。

sentences.en: So if you wanted to go through sand or you may find yourself in deep snow or dirt,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想穿过沙地，或者你发现自己身处深雪或泥土中，

sentences.en: the entire system is now going to recalculate and adjust the suspension acceleration brakes to make that the best experience.
sentences.zh: 整个系统现在将重新计算并调整悬挂、加速和刹车，以确保带来最佳体验。

sentences.en: Now, when you're in multi-terrain select, you then hit your panoramic view monitor and you're now seeing this bird's eye view.
sentences.zh: 现在，当你开启多地形选择系统时，再按下全景监控按钮，就能看到这种上帝视角了。

sentences.en: It's called the multi-terrain monitor.
sentences.zh: 它被称为多地形监控系统。

sentences.en: So this is an additional view where you're getting really full, clear view of where you are, right?
sentences.zh: 这是一个额外的视角，让你能非常全面、清晰地了解自己所处的位置，对吧？

sentences.en: You might be, if you're overlanding on that trail, this may be a side of a cliff, right?
sentences.zh: 如果你正在那条小径上进行越野探险，这可能就是悬崖的一侧，对吧？

sentences.en: Or this could be, this is in front of you.
sentences.zh: 或者这可能是你前方的情况。

sentences.en: This may be a tree stump right here.
sentences.zh: 这儿可能就是一个树桩。

sentences.en: So when I go out off-roading, overlanding, having visibility on your car is like the biggest thing you could ask for.
sentences.zh: 所以当我出去越野、探险时，能看清车身周围的情况简直是最大的诉求。

sentences.en: And to that end, I have to mention my favorite feature, which I think exemplifies the 2024 Lexus GX.
sentences.zh: 说到这一点，我必须提到我最喜欢的功能，我认为它完美体现了2024款雷克萨斯GX的精髓。

sentences.en: It's so simple and in true 99PI fashion, it's something that is not fancy and could be totally overlooked,
sentences.zh: 它非常简单，而且很有99PI的风格，它并不花哨，甚至完全可能被忽视，

sentences.en: but it tells you something about all the thought that went into the GX.
sentences.zh: 但它向你传达了GX在设计上所倾注的心血。

sentences.en: And that is the shape of the front hood.
sentences.zh: 那就是前引擎盖的形状。

sentences.en: One of the things that frustrates me about the big car that I have that fits all the kids that Joy mostly drives
sentences.zh: 我那辆大车平时主要是Joy在开，用来接送所有孩子，但有一点让我很苦恼，

sentences.en: is I can't judge where the end of the hood is.
sentences.zh: 就是我无法判断引擎盖的尽头在哪里。

sentences.en: It kind of slopes down and I end up thinking I'm way closer to whatever it is in front of me than I actually am.
sentences.zh: 它有点向下倾斜，导致我总以为自己离前面的东西比实际距离近得多。

sentences.en: It's absurd.
sentences.zh: 这太荒谬了。

sentences.en: I think I'm two feet away from a parked car and I'm actually six feet away.
sentences.zh: 我以为离停着的车只有两英尺，其实还有六英尺远。

sentences.en: But this new Lexus elegantly solved my problem.
sentences.zh: 但这款新款雷克萨斯优雅地解决了我的问题。

sentences.en: The hood vents there, you see how they're higher, the indentations up top?
sentences.zh: 你看那里的引擎盖通风口，看到它们更高、顶部的凹槽了吗？

sentences.en: That is designed so that when you're off-roading, that you have good reference of where the end of your vehicle is.
sentences.zh: 那是专门设计的，这样当你越野时，就能很好地参照车辆的边界位置。

sentences.en: And paying attention to that need and solving for that function made the whole vehicle more striking.
sentences.zh: 关注到这一需求并解决这一功能问题，让整辆车看起来更加引人注目。

sentences.en: That right there is part of the look.
sentences.zh: 这正是外观的一部分。

sentences.en: You can see it from the outside that gives it that very kind of modular, aggressive stance.
sentences.zh: 从外面看，它赋予了车辆那种非常模块化、充满侵略性的姿态。

sentences.en: It's not so rounded maybe where you might see in the current generation.
sentences.zh: 它不像现款车型那样圆润。

sentences.en: So the design solves the problem that makes the GX more functional in more places.
sentences.zh: 所以这种设计解决了问题，使GX在更多场景下更具实用性。

sentences.en: And that affects the look.
sentences.zh: 这也影响了外观。

sentences.en: And that look makes the GX stand out.

sentences.zh: 这一切都归功于设计的迭代，以及雷克萨斯设计师、工程师与

sentences.en: But when you're out there in the middle of nowhere, a capable, reliable vehicle isn't the only thing you need.

sentences.en: you can still turn on Sirius XM satellite radio and hear the voice of Rachel Steele.
sentences.zh: 你依然可以打开Sirius XM卫星广播，听到Rachel Steele的声音。

sentences.en: My name is Rachel Steele, and I am a DJ on two classic rock channels,
sentences.zh: 我叫Rachel Steele，是两个经典摇滚频道的DJ，

sentences.en: classic vinyl channel 26 and classic rewind channel 25.
sentences.zh: 分别是26频道的经典黑胶频道和25频道的经典重温频道。

sentences.en: A huge classic rock fan, huge rock fan in general.
sentences.zh: 我是一个超级经典摇滚迷，也是一个超级摇滚乐迷。

sentences.en: So tell me, what is the difference between classic rewind and classic vinyl?
sentences.zh: 那么告诉我，经典重温和经典黑胶之间有什么区别？

sentences.en: So we consider the classic rock time period to be from the early 60s through the late 80s.
sentences.zh: 我们认为经典摇滚时期是从60年代初到80年代末。

sentences.en: So classic vinyl, we cover the early 60s through the early 70s,
sentences.zh: 经典黑胶频道涵盖了60年代初到70年代初，

sentences.en: and then we pick it up with the mid-70s to the late 80s on classic rewind.
sentences.zh: 然后经典重温频道接着涵盖70年代中期到80年代末。

sentences.en: Tell me, like, when you turn on channel 25, what is the reward waiting for you?
sentences.zh: 告诉我，当你打开25频道时，会有什么样的奖励在等着你？

sentences.en: I think with classic vinyl and classic rewind both, you get the ability to reminisce,
sentences.zh: 我认为无论是经典黑胶还是经典重温，你都能获得怀旧的机会，

sentences.en: you know, especially going back to those early days and hearing songs that you grew up with.
sentences.zh: 你知道，特别是回到那些早期的日子，听到你从小听到大的歌曲。

sentences.en: It's always comfort.
sentences.zh: 这总是一种慰藉。

sentences.en: I think I always try to reach the listeners in a comfortable way.
sentences.zh: 我想我总是试图以一种舒适的方式触达听众。

sentences.en: In the car, I feel like I am a companion.
sentences.zh: 在车里，我觉得自己是一个陪伴者。

sentences.en: I think all DJs are a companion.
sentences.zh: 我认为所有的DJ都是陪伴者。

sentences.en: And what we have in common is the music.
sentences.zh: 而我们共同的纽带就是音乐。

sentences.en: So I love to be able to share stories and bring these artists to life.
sentences.zh: 所以我喜欢分享故事，让这些艺术家鲜活起来。

sentences.en: And I think the car is the perfect opportunity to do that.
sentences.zh: 我认为汽车是实现这一点的绝佳场所。

sentences.en: You know, people kick back and relax.

sentences.en: And now me and Joy back out on the street in Chicago.
sentences.zh: 现在我和Joy回到了芝加哥的街头。

sentences.en: So this is an office building in the old Montgomery Ward complex.
sentences.zh: 这是一座位于旧蒙哥马利·沃德大楼群里的办公楼。

sentences.en: It was designed by Minoru Yamasaki.
sentences.zh: 它由山崎实设计。

sentences.en: And I have to admit, when I lived here, I rarely looked up at this building.
sentences.zh: 我必须承认，我住在这里的时候，很少抬头看这栋楼。

sentences.en: It's a standard modern sort of cereal box with graph paper on it.
sentences.zh: 它就像一个标准的现代麦片盒，上面印着方格纸。

sentences.en: But it does have these notable, like, white concrete columns on the four corners.
sentences.zh: 但它确实有那些引人注目的白色混凝土柱子，位于四个角上。

sentences.en: It makes it, you know, kind of a little more chunky.
sentences.zh: 这让它看起来，你知道，稍微厚实了一些。

sentences.en: It's still sleek, but chunky.
sentences.zh: 它依然流畅，但很厚实。

sentences.en: And I pass it every day on my way home from work from WBC.
sentences.zh: 我每天从WBC下班回家的路上都会经过它。

sentences.en: I walk past this over the river and then catch the blue line home to Logan Square.
sentences.zh: 我走过河边，然后搭乘蓝线地铁回家去洛根广场。

sentences.en: And part of the reason you can ignore it is there's, like, like you've seen,
sentences.zh: 你之所以会忽略它，部分原因正如你所见，

sentences.en: there's, like, so many cool buildings in Chicago.
sentences.zh: 芝加哥有太多很酷的建筑了。

sentences.en: It's kind of hard to stand out as a skyscraper in Chicago.
sentences.zh: 在芝加哥，作为摩天大楼想要脱颖而出真的很难。

sentences.en: But regardless, even with this sort of blue-green tinted glass, it just didn't grab me.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，即使有这种蓝绿色的玻璃，它就是没能吸引我。

sentences.en: And then I took the Chicago Architecture Center's boat tour.
sentences.zh: 后来我参加了芝加哥建筑中心的游船之旅。

sentences.en: And the docent told me why this building has those thick concrete corner supports.
sentences.zh: 导游告诉我为什么这栋楼有那些厚实的混凝土角柱。

sentences.en: First, they open up the floor plan so that you can make your office as open in areas you want
sentences.zh: 首先，它们腾出了楼层空间，这样你就可以根据需要让办公室尽可能开放，

sentences.en: because there's no internal walls that need to be there.
sentences.zh: 因为不需要内部墙壁。

sentences.en: But most importantly, to me anyway, was that the Montgomery Ward Company
sentences.zh: 但对我来说最重要的是，蒙哥马利·沃德公司

sentences.en: prided itself on having this sort of egalitarian hierarchy.
sentences.zh: 以拥有这种平等主义的等级制度而自豪。

sentences.en: And they didn't want executives fighting over who got a corner office.
sentences.zh: 他们不想让高管们为了争夺转角办公室而打架。

sentences.en: So they designed a building without any possibility of a corner office at all.
sentences.zh: 所以他们设计了一栋根本不可能有转角办公室的建筑。

sentences.en: It's now been converted into luxury condos, and it's simply known as the Montgomery.
sentences.zh: 它现在已被改建成豪华公寓，简称为“蒙哥马利”。

sentences.en: And I bet the developers, like, hate those thick columns with all their heart,
sentences.zh: 我敢打赌，开发商肯定打心底里讨厌那些厚重的柱子，

sentences.en: you know, wishing they could sell a corner condo that doesn't exiSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们肯定希望自己能卖出根本不存在的转角公寓。

sentences.en: But that story makes me love this building.
sentences.zh: 但那个故事让我爱上了这栋建筑。

sentences.en: And so I think it's great.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为它很棒。

sentences.en: That story has stayed with me for years.
sentences.zh: 那个故事多年来一直萦绕在我心头。

sentences.en: And I've taken the Chicago Architecture boat tour, you know,
sentences.zh: 我已经参加过芝加哥建筑游船之旅，你知道，

sentences.en: now five or six times we're going to do it.
sentences.zh: 现在已经是第五或第六次了，我们还要再去。

sentences.en: Tomorrow, it's really, really stunning.
sentences.zh: 明天，它真的非常非常迷人。

sentences.en: And because of that tour, I think of this as one of my favorite buildings.
sentences.zh: 因为那次旅行，我认为这是我最喜欢的建筑之一。

sentences.en: And keep in mind, this is a building I rarely even bothered to crane my neck to look at.
sentences.zh: 请记住，这栋楼我以前甚至很少费心去抬头看一眼。

sentences.en: I really did pass it daily.
sentences.zh: 我确实每天都经过它。

sentences.en: But I've learned to appreciate its aesthetics more as I've retold that story again and again.
sentences.zh: 但随着我一次又一次地重述那个故事，我学会了更多地欣赏它的美学。

sentences.en: And it's why I contend that story is the universal language of design, even more than aesthetics.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我坚持认为故事是设计的通用语言，甚至比美学更重要。

sentences.en: Like, don't get me wrong, like, I love pretty things.
sentences.zh: 别误会，我喜欢漂亮的东西。

sentences.en: But sometimes, you know, prejudice and bias and ignorance and taste get in the way of me loving a brilliant structure with a great story to tell.
sentences.zh: 但有时，你知道，偏见、成见、无知和品味会阻碍我爱上一座拥有精彩故事的杰出建筑。

sentences.en: And that revelation led to 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 而那个启示促成了《99%隐形》节目的诞生。

sentences.en: So this building is in many ways why I do what I do today.
sentences.zh: 所以这栋建筑在很多方面成就了今天的我。

sentences.en: I love that.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个故事。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.zh: 所以你还没怎么在芝加哥待过。

sentences.en: I haven't.

sentences.zh: 我之前只来过一次，还没真正四处逛逛或探索过。

sentences.zh: 这里很不错，不是吗？

sentences.zh: 我很期待那个游船之旅。

sentences.en: Yes.

sentences.en: It really is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So you'll hear maybe some of these stories again.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能还会再听到一些这样的故事。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。
